text: # GEO report: Millstone Bakery **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 100/100, Strong Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. This is a small static HTML site of 4 pages (home, breads, classes and a private members page), and I read all of them. Every applicable rule is Clear, read from code. Nothing was measured on a live site. The score covers technical readiness only. Most of the value left is in the content ideas under "Worth considering". ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first Nothing is broken, so these are the biggest remaining unknowns and gaps. The first two are not scored. ### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your host or CDN - **Why it matters:** Code can't show whether a firewall or CDN blocks the search crawlers your `robots.txt` allows. - **Where:** `robots.txt:1` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100 if it comes back clear. The code score doesn't include this check. ### 2. Describe the business in machine-readable form - **Why it matters:** The name, address and hours appear nowhere in the site, so tools have nothing to quote about the business itself. - **Where:** `index.html:9` (the blank line in `` where it would go) - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100. Structured data (JSON-LD) isn't scored here. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and within size limits | Clear | `robots.txt:1-8` | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can access the site | Clear | `robots.txt:1-3`; only GPTBot (a training crawler) is blocked, which matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"` | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 sitemap routes; `members/index.html:9` is a deliberate noindex and isn't in the sitemap | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | 4 of 4 routes, all on `https://www.millstonebakery.example` | | GEO-003 | Content present in server HTML | Clear | Plain static HTML | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt:8` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` present | Clear | 4 of 4 routes, each with its own title and description; `lang="en"` on every page | | GEO-016 | Key routes reachable by real links | Clear | `` nav on every page | | GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Only element-level `data-nosnippet` at `breads.html:16`, which is deliberate | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | The only image has `alt` (`index.html:16`); read 4 pages | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | None present; never scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not an app; never scored | ## Other problems found - **Image file not in the repo:** `index.html:16`: ``. No `img/` folder is tracked here. If it isn't served from elsewhere, the image is broken, so add the file. ## Worth considering - **Add LocalBusiness or Bakery structured data:** `index.html:6`: `Millstone Bakery, sourdough in York`. Nothing states the address, hours or contact details in text or machine-readable form. Add them to the page, then label them with JSON-LD. - **Say what "over twenty loaves" are:** `breads.html:15`: `Over twenty loaves through the week, including our seeded rye and the country white.` The page names only two loaves. List all of them with a short description and which days each is baked. - **Give each bread its own page:** `breads.html:15`. The loaves could each have their own address, such as `/breads/seeded-rye`, which would give people and tools a specific page to find and quote. - **Put class details in text:** `classes.html:15`: `Learn to bake sourdough in a small group. Book early...` There are no dates, prices, class length, group size or booking link. A visitor's first questions go unanswered. - **Explain the ordering:** `index.html:15`: `Pre-order for weekend collection.` The page doesn't say how to pre-order, the cut-off time or the pickup location. Add them as text, and link to a page that has them. - **Link the pages to each other:** `classes.html:15` and `breads.html:15` link onward only through the shared nav. Add contextual links, for example from classes to the breads you bake in them. - **Add `` dates:** `sitemap.xml:3`: `https://www.millstonebakery.example/`. If you know when pages last changed, dates help crawlers prioritise recrawling. - **Add social-sharing tags:** `index.html:7` has no `og:title`, `og:description` or `og:image`. They control how links to the site look when shared. - **Add a custom 404 page:** the repo has no 404 file, so wrong addresses show whatever the host defaults to. A friendly page linking back to the breads and classes would help visitors who land on a dead address. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have an access log, `geopilot logs ` checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Server responses:** real status codes, redirects, and headers such as `X-Robots-Tag` need a live check. Whether `/breads.html` and the other URLs answer 200 is one example. Give me a URL and I'll run one. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools to find the site, as `geo.config.json` says (`aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`). - Blocking GPTBot (`robots.txt:5-6`) and keeping `/members/` out of search are deliberate choices, so I haven't suggested changing them. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 2. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
